title: Adaptive Kernel-Weighted Phase Slicer for latency-sensitive fairness
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: As we onboard larger customer workloads and more heterogeneous kernels (FP16 fused kernels, int8/4x4 quantized kernels, and attention-sparse variants), current phase-splitting schedulers either prioritize throughput (by grouping large batches) or latency (by hedging small requests), but they lack a unified mechanism that accounts for kernel performance differences and attention cost signals. This results in two failure modes: (1) latency-sensitive tenants suffering long tails when their small requests get fused into large kernel paths optimized for throughput, and (2) throughput-optimized customers experiencing throughput regressions as we over-hedge small phases onto expensive sparse-attn kernels.

Goal: Implement an Adaptive Kernel-Weighted Phase Slicer (AKW-PS) that: (a) uses per-kernel latency/cost profiles + attention pattern hints to score and slice prefill/decode phases, (b) enforces per-tenant latency budgets with token-credit fairness, and (c) dynamically steers slices to appropriate kernel classes (fast low-batch kernels vs high-throughput fused kernels) with minimal fragmentation overhead.
background: We already collect kernel microbenchmarks (latency vs sequence length and batch size) and attention density estimates from the tokenizer/first-pass analyzer. Previous tickets focused on phase fairness and microphase partitioners but didn't integrate kernel selection signals or token-credit enforcement targeted at tenant-level SLAs. This ticket bridges kernel-aware cost signals and tenant fairness enforcement in the slicer.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler assigns phase slices with kernel-class hints in >90% of sampled requests according to kernel scoring (validated in devbench)
End-to-end p50/p95 latency for latency-tier tenants does not regress >5% vs baseline when AKW-PS is enabled (measured on canary cluster)
Throughput for throughput-tier tenants remains within 95% of baseline for steady-state workloads
Token-credit accounting prevents starvation: no tenant loses >10% of SLA throughput for more than 15 minutes under mixed load in perf test
Feature toggle and rollout flags exist in control plane; rollback restores previous scheduler deterministically
decision_log: 2025-02-20: Choose soft-hints for kernel selection (score influences routing but does not veto) to avoid brittle build-time coupling with kernels
2025-02-25: Use token-credit ledger per-tenant (leaky-bucket) instead of strict priority queues to make fairness composable with autoscaling bursts
2025-02-28: Implement attention-density probe in prefill analyzer; do not rely on full attention computation to avoid probe overhead
updates: 2025-02-19 - Asha: Spike completed — microbench harness extended to emit per-kernel cost curves (latency vs batch/seq). Observed that quantized kernels have a 1.8-2.5x latency variance at small batch sizes.

2025-02-22 - Diego: Prototype AKW scoring function checked in (internal branch) — uses weighted sum: alpha*kernel_latency_est + beta*attention_density + gamma*tenant_lat_budget. Needs tuning of weights.
2025-02-26 - SRE consult: Load test plan added. Canary cluster reserved for 24hr mixed-tenant run. Watchlist: p99 tail for latency-tier tenants and GPU utilization skew.

2025-03-03 - Diego: Integration test failing on fragmentation case — many tiny slices created for multi-tenant long prefill requests. Adding compaction pass to merge contiguous tiny slices when kernel hint matches.

2025-03-04 - Asha: Initial perf run on devbench: latency-tier tenant p95 improved 12% on synthetic conversational workload; throughput-tier baseline dropped ~3% for bursty tails. Moving to canary next week.

rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag; 2) Devbench perf + unit tests; 3) Canary cluster with 2 latency-tier customers for 48hr; 4) Gradual percentage rollout (10%->50%->100%) with auto-rollback on p95 SLO breach
risks: Over-fragmentation: naive slicing could create many tiny GPU kernels increasing overhead
Score miscalibration: incorrect weighting could bias routes and cause unfair throttling
Instrumentation: need accurate kernel cost curves per HW revision; stale metrics cause bad routing
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring, simulation harness to replay 24h of production traces with mixed tenants, canary run with SLO alerts wired to pager. Include fuzz tests that vary kernel latency curves by +/-20%.
notes: If AKW-PS proves effective, follow-up work: (a) persist preferred kernel hints in model catalog, (b) expose per-route affinity overrides in Console, (c) autoscale knobs to allow temporary over-provisioning for latency guarantees.
